claims.text: An actively learned MTP combined with adaptive DFPT corrections can accurately compute fusion free energies and high-temperature thermodynamic properties for equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
MTPs can be actively learned from DFT configurations.
MTPs offer a favorable balance between DFT-level accuracy and computational cost in multicomponent refractory alloys.
Using an MTP for molecular-dynamics sampling decouples sampling from the expensive direct ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations.
The MTP defines an effective high-dimensional free-energy surface that captures anharmonicity and vibrational contributions in both solid and liquid CoCrFeMnNi.
Adaptive DFPT corrections can refine electronic-structure and electron–vibration-coupling contributions during finite-temperature sampling.
Online deviations in local energies or forces can serve as reliable triggers for applying DFPT corrections.
Applying DFPT only when error indicators exceed predefined thresholds will retain electron–vibration coupling and other fine-scale corrections in ensemble-averaged free energies.
The proposed workflow will reduce computational cost by up to one order of magnitude relative to full ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed workflow will reduce computational cost by up to one order of magnitude relative to TOR-TILD.
The workflow will predict phase free energies within approximately 5% of explicit ab initio benchmarks.
The workflow will predict latent heat and melting entropy within approximately 5% of explicit ab initio benchmarks.
Explicit ab initio molecular dynamics is accurate but significantly more computationally expensive than the proposed workflow.
TOR-TILD is significantly more computationally expensive and less applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys than the proposed workflow.
The melting-point region of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is approximately 1200–1600 K.
The proposed study is restricted to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, both solid and liquid, over 1200–1600 K.
Configurations from both solid and liquid phases along the fusion pathway will be sampled.
Transfer of the workflow to other compositions or temperature regimes may require additional validation.
